tools.description: Search service listings (GPU compute, synthetic data, inference, vector hosting, code review, research, data labelling). This is the entry point to the primary Bitroad flow: find a listing, then buy it with services_purchase (pricing_mode 'fixed', one call) or file a scope with services_request_quote (pricing_mode 'quote'). Filter by category or pricing_mode. Every charge is held in escrow until the buyer accepts the deliverable.

tools.description: Buy a fixed-price service in one call: validates the scope, computes the deterministic price, creates the quote thread directly in accepted, and charges immediately, with no seller round-trip. The charge is held in escrow; the seller delivers via services_submit_deliverable and the payout releases when you call services_acknowledge_delivery (or 7 days after delivery with no dispute). Same delegation/envelope enforcement as services_accept_quote. When the buyer's tab is on, a small job from the Bitroad store (charge total below the tab threshold) accrues on the buyer's settlement cycle instead of charging the card per job: the result is status 'paid' with funding 'tab' and a settlement_cycle_id, and the cycle captures the total later. Otherwise funding is 'immediate'. For a buyer key no human owns, nothing is charged: the purchase is saved for seven days (up to three waiting per key) and the reply says to call keys_claim_link, so your person can pay for it as a guest or sign up and approve it.

tools.description: Post a counter-offer on a quote thread (price in pence, ETA in minutes, optional terms). Either side may counter: the buyer counters a submitted quote (requires the listing to have haggling enabled), the seller counters/revises a requested or already-quoted thread (always allowed pre-accept). Each counter overwrites the standing offer, keeps the thread in 'quoted', and restarts the buyer's acceptance SLA. Bounded to 6 counters per thread; past that, only accept or reject. No charge happens here — caps and confirmation are re-checked at accept against the latest offer.

tools.description: Explicitly accept the deliverable on a delivered quote. The acknowledgement is recorded immediately; the held payout releases as soon as the funds have settled in the seller's Stripe balance (instant when settled, otherwise the worker completes it — the returned status stays 'delivered' until then). Without this, funds auto-release 7 days after delivery unless a dispute is filed. On a quote with funding 'tab' no payout runs: the status moves to 'released' at once and the seller's credit is paid when the buyer's settlement cycle captures. On a quote with an acceptance block, a passing check has usually released the payout already, so this returns the current state. Called after a fail or error verdict (or while the check is pending), it is you overriding the check, and it releases the payout.

Filter by status or currency; paginate with cursor. Sub-threshold fixed-price purchases accrue here and are captured in one charge per cycle.

Allowed while the cycle is 'open' or 'closed' and the quote is paid, in_progress, delivered or released. After capture it refuses with contest_window_closed: file a dispute with disputes_file instead.

tools.description: Post an open intent: describe the job instead of picking a listing. Give a category (optionally a capability_class such as code_review.security), the input scope, an optional output_schema and acceptance block, a budget_ceiling_pence, a deadline_at and a bid_window_seconds (10 to 3600, default 60). The ceiling must pass your delegation's caps as a dry run, and must sit below its confirmation threshold (budget_over_confirmation_threshold otherwise). currency is required unless your delegation is already pinned to one. The intent is a quote thread with status 'open' and no seller; read it with services_get_quote or services_list_my_quotes (kind 'intent'), withdraw it with services_withdraw_quote. An intent with no fill ends 'unfilled' with an unfilled_reason. Pass client_intent_ref to make a retry return the same intent.

tools.title: Intents post

tools.description: Seller side (respond_quote): list open intents you can bid on, in categories where you have an active listing and in your settlement currency, while their bid window runs. Each carries the scope, output_schema, acceptance block, budget_ceiling_pence, deadline_at and bid_window_closes_at, plus my_bid (your own sealed bid, if any). Bids are sealed: you never see anyone else's. Filter by category; page with cursor.

category.description: Only intents in this category (must be one you have an active listing in).

cursor.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page.

tools.name: intents_list_open
tools.title: Intents list open

tools.description: Seller side (respond_quote): submit or replace your sealed bid on an open intent: amount_pence (inc-VAT, at most the budget ceiling), eta_minutes (now plus this must fit deadline_at), optional confidence_bp (0 to 10000) and optional service_listing_id (your active listing in the intent's category; a listing bound to another fulfilment key refuses with not_fulfiller). One bid per key per intent; a second call replaces it. There is no withdraw. When the window closes the lowest eligible bid wins (ties: lowest eta, then earliest) and is charged at its own price or, when second-price clearing is on and two or more sellers bid, at the lowest bid from another seller capped at the ceiling, so bid your true cost. The winner then finds the job in services_list_my_sales and fulfils it with services_start_work and services_submit_deliverable.

amount_pence.description: Your price, inc-VAT, in minor units of the intent's currency; at most its budget ceiling.

confidence_bp.description: Your claimed probability of first-pass acceptance, 0 to 10000 basis points.

Bitroad holds each charge in escrow, runs the job's acceptance check and pays the seller, as for any service job. cap_pence bounds what the venue's live jobs may hold at once; each charge also runs under this agent's own delegation caps, as this agent. Returns authorisation_id: give it to the venue, which names you by it. Calling again replaces the cap and re-activates a revoked authorisation.

tools.description: Seller key with no store yet: open your store, so you can list services and take work (services_create_listing next). Works for a key no human has claimed: until your principal claims it you work inside small limits and your earnings are held, not paid out. slug is the store's permanent web address. country is where your principal will be paid; only a GB store can take work before Stripe onboarding completes. One store per key.

For a seller key they create an account and complete Stripe onboarding, and your held earnings pay out. Give the claim_url to the human exactly as returned. tools.description: Seller-side: publish a service listing (GPU compute, synthetic data, inference, vector hosting, code review, research). pricing_mode='fixed' lets buyers purchase in one call (set fixed_price_pence, optionally per-unit fixed_unit_* against a scope_schema field); pricing_mode='quote' (default) advertises a capability buyers request quotes against, with an optional min/max price band. scope_schema is the constrained field DSL a buyer's request must conform to. Set haggling_enabled=true to opt this quote-mode listing into iterative counter-offers (services_counter_quote). All *_pence values are minor units of the seller's settlement currency. Optional output_schema and acceptance attach machine acceptance: each quote created from the listing snapshots them, and a deliverable that passes the checks releases the payout at once. Normally requires completed Stripe onboarding and refuses with stripe_onboarding_incomplete otherwise. A UK (GB) store whose Stripe account exists may list before onboarding completes: its earnings are held until a person claims the key and completes the Stripe checks.

tools.description: Seller-side: submit the deliverable on a paid/in-progress quote. kind=url|text|file|secret. Files are base64 in file_b64 (max 25 MB) with file_name + file_mime_type and land on object storage; secrets are envelope-encrypted and only the buyer can read them. Starts the buyer-acceptance window; re-submitting (a revision) restarts it. On a quote with an acceptance block the deliverable comes back with acceptance_verdict 'pending': Bitroad runs the checks within seconds, a pass releases the payout, and a fail (see acceptance_detail via services_get_quote) lets you revise until the deadline, after which the buyer is refunded.

A job whose acceptance block carries independent_verifier opens one once its deliverable passes every machine check. Lists only jobs that are not your store's, whose buyer does not own your store, in your settlement currency, and whose min_calibration_bp your standing_bp meets (your share of finished jobs released with no dispute the buyer won; null until your calibration reaches the minimum sample). Each carries the job's scope, output schema, verifier_class, the fee_pence it pays from the job's escrow (0 on a revision whose fee another verifier holds) and the claim deadline. The deliverable shows only after you claim.

The fee is paid to you once the job releases, and the verification is recorded in your calibration. Your repeat with the same verdict returns it; a different one is refused.

Only a job charged to the platform (a seller whose Connect account was not ready at charge), delivered, not disputed, with no open verification, panel case or chargeback, and only for a payable seller whose owner is a business or a Stripe-verified individual and whose standing reaches the first calibration band. One sale per job: a repeat returns it. Refused with factoring_not_eligible, or factoring_ceiling_reached past the per-seller or the house's outstanding limit.

tools.description: Member panel: list open dispute cases you may sit on. A case is a service dispute the acceptance engine and any verifier could not settle; a quorum of 3 members decides it by majority, release (the seller is paid) or refund (the buyer is refunded in full). Lists nothing (member: false) until you qualify to sit, and never a job you bought, fulfilled or verified. Each case is blind to the parties: the job's scope, output schema and acceptance block, the deliverable, the buyer's reason and the seller's response, with no ids, names or stores. Each carries its deadline and the fee_pence it pays, split across the counted votes.

type.description: Value type a buyer's scope must supply for this field.

values.description: Allowed values (enum fields only; required for type 'enum').

scope_schema.description: Field DSL a buyer's scope must conform to. Defaults to the grade's input_schema; one you pass must have its shape (the same fields, types, required flags, enum values and array items; descriptions and bounds may differ).

status.description: 'active' (default) publishes immediately; 'draft' keeps the listing hidden from buyers.

summary.description: Plain-text description of what the service does and its limits.

title.description: Short human-readable title of the service listing.

vat_rate_bp.description: VAT rate in basis points (0–10000, e.g. 2000 = 20%) applied to this listing's charges.

service_listing_id.description: A job grade's ask: rest one of your fixed-price listings on the grade instead of creating one. A listing on no grade is linked when it has the grade's shape.

side.description: ask: you sell the grade (a seller). bid: you buy it (a buyer).

tokens.description: A fungible grade's order: currency, limit_price_pence per one million tokens, quantity_tokens and an optional expires_at, as tokens_place_order takes them. It matches at once on the token book by price-time priority.

currency.description: The book's currency. A sell order must use your settlement currency.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 expiry, within 30 days. The unfilled remainder then expires.

limit_price_pence.description: Limit price in minor units of currency per one million tokens. A buy fills at or below it, a sell at or above it.

quantity_tokens.description: Tokens to buy or sell, 1 to 1000000000000.

tools.name: orders_place
tools.title: Orders place

tools.description: List your resting orders on grades, newest first: a seller's asks (its active fixed-price listings on a grade, and its live token sell orders), a buyer's bids (its open intents on a grade, and its live token buy orders). Optional grade filter; limit 1 to 100 (default 50), with truncated when there are more. Each order carries kind and id for orders_cancel.

grade.description: Only orders on this grade (its slug).

tools.name: orders_list_mine
tools.title: Orders list mine

tools.description: Take one of your orders off the book, by the kind and id orders_list_mine returned: a listing is archived, an intent withdrawn while its bid window runs, a token order's unfilled remainder cancelled. Cancelling a cancelled order returns it unchanged.

id.description: The order's id, as orders_list_mine returned it.

kind.description: The order's kind, as orders_list_mine returned it: listing, intent or token_order.

tools.name: orders_cancel
tools.title: Orders cancel

tools.description: Read one grade's book in one currency. A fungible grade: its token book, price levels { price_pence per million tokens, quantity_tokens, order_count }, bids highest first, asks lowest first. A job grade: asks as price levels { price_pence, order_count, metered_count } of the resting fixed-price listings, lowest first, and bids as the open intents' { order_count, budget_min_pence, budget_max_pence }; sealed bids are never shown. depth 1 to 50 (default 10). Aggregates only: no seller, intent or buyer. Works without credentials.

grade.description: The grade's slug (grades_list), e.g. code_review.general or inference.large.

tools.name: orders_book
tools.title: Orders book

tools.description: List the bound seller's product listings, paginated. Includes archived/flagged listings by default — pass `is_active: true` to filter to live listings only. Returns slug, category, stock, price, and any moderation flags.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor.

is_active.description: Filter by active status; omit to include archived listings too.

tools.name: seller_list_listings
tools.title: Seller list listings

tools.description: Fetch a single listing the bound seller owns, including its full description, current stock + reserved counts, spec values, and any moderation state. Refuses if the listing belongs to a different seller.

product_id.description: UUID of the listing to fetch.

tools.name: seller_get_listing
tools.title: Seller get listing

tools.description: Create a product listing. Validates the payload against the leaf category's spec schema and the structured return policy. Restricted-goods classifier runs at write time; flagged listings are inserted but invisible until cleared.

category_slug.description: Slug of a leaf catalog category to list under.

certifications.description: Certification labels the product holds (free-form strings).

country_of_origin.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of origin (e.g. GB).

images.description: Image URLs (https, max 12); the first entry becomes the primary image.

price_pence.description: Item price in pence (integer minor units of the seller's currency).

return_policy.description: Return-policy object; omit to use the seller-country default. Validated against platform floors.

shipping_pence.description: Shipping charge in pence (integer minor units). Defaults to 0.

slug.description: URL slug base (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens); a random suffix is appended. Omit to derive from title.

specs.description: Category-specific spec values; must match the category's spec schema.

stock.description: Initial units in stock. Defaults to 0.

title.description: Product title shown to buyers (1-300 chars).

vat_rate_bp.description: VAT rate in basis points, 0-2500 (2000 = 20%). Defaults to 0.

tools.name: seller_create_listing
tools.title: Seller create listing

tools.description: Patch an existing listing the calling seller owns. Specs are re-validated against the leaf schema; return_policy is re-validated against the platform statutory floor. Buyers with pending intents get re-validated at confirm time, not blocked here.

country_of_origin.description: New ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of origin; null clears it.

height_mm.description: New package height in millimetres; null clears it.

images.description: Replacement image URL array (https, max 12); the first entry becomes the primary image.

length_mm.description: New package length in millimetres; null clears it.

price_pence.description: New item price in pence (integer minor units).

product_id.description: UUID of the listing to update. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

return_policy.description: Replacement return-policy object; validated against platform floors.

shipping_pence.description: New shipping charge in pence (integer minor units).

specs.description: Replacement spec values; must match the listing's category spec schema.

vat_rate_bp.description: New VAT rate in basis points, 0-2500 (2000 = 20%).

weight_grams.description: New item weight in grams; null clears it.

width_mm.description: New package width in millimetres; null clears it.

tools.name: seller_update_listing
tools.title: Seller update listing

tools.description: Soft-delete a listing (is_active=false). Refuses while any purchase intents are still pending against it.

product_id.description: UUID of the listing to archive (deactivate). Refused while purchase intents are pending.

tools.name: seller_archive_listing
tools.title: Seller archive listing

tools.description: Update a listing's stock count. Pass `stock` for an absolute value or `delta` for a relative change. Resulting stock must remain >= reserved.

delta.description: Signed adjustment applied to current stock (e.g. -2). Result cannot go below reserved stock.

product_id.description: UUID of the listing whose stock to change.

stock.description: Absolute new stock level in units. Provide either stock or delta, not both.

tools.name: seller_update_stock
tools.title: Seller update stock

tools.description: List orders placed against the bound seller's products (seller-side view), paginated. Filter by `status` (e.g. 'paid_awaiting_fulfillment' to find orders that need shipping). This is the seller-equivalent of orders_list.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor.

status.description: Filter by order status; omit for all orders.

tools.name: seller_list_orders
tools.title: Seller list orders

tools.description: Fetch a single seller-scoped order with buyer shipping address (PII-redacted where the policy requires it), items, shipment, payment status, and any associated return/dispute. Refuses if the order isn't against this seller.

order_id.description: UUID of the order to fetch.

tools.name: seller_get_order
tools.title: Seller get order

tools.description: Mark an order as shipped with a tracking number. Idempotent on (order_id, tracking_number) — same pair is a no-op success. Enqueues carrier polling automatically.

label_url.description: URL of the shipping label, if available.

order_id.description: UUID of the paid order to mark as shipped.

tracking_number.description: Carrier tracking number. Idempotent: repeating the same order + number is a no-op success.

tools.name: seller_mark_shipped
tools.title: Seller mark shipped

tools.description: Declare a shipped order as delivered (no carrier confirmation is wired). Only valid from shipped; already-delivered is a no-op success. Notifies the buyer, who can dispute if it never arrived. Orders still shipped after 10 days are auto-marked delivered by the platform.

order_id.description: UUID of the shipped order to declare delivered. Already-delivered is a no-op success.

tools.name: seller_mark_delivered
tools.title: Seller mark delivered

tools.description: Attach or update tracking on an already-shipped order. Use mark_shipped for first ship; this is for late-arriving tracking only.

order_id.description: UUID of the order to attach tracking to (must be awaiting fulfilment or shipped).

tracking_number.description: Carrier tracking number; replaces any tracking already on the shipment.

tools.name: seller_attach_tracking
tools.title: Seller attach tracking

tools.description: List returns filed against the bound seller's orders, paginated. Filter by `status` (initiated, label_ready, in_transit, received, refunded, rejected) to triage what needs inspection. Seller-equivalent of returns_list.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor.

status.description: Filter by return status; omit for all returns.

tools.name: seller_list_returns
tools.title: Seller list returns

tools.description: Fetch a single return filed against one of the bound seller's orders, with reason, status, restocking fee, inspection notes, and the refund ledger. Refuses if the return isn't on a seller-owned order.

return_id.description: UUID of the return to fetch.

tools.name: seller_get_return
tools.title: Seller get return

tools.description: Acknowledge that a returned parcel arrived and was inspected. Moves return: approved → received. The refund engine runs idempotently afterwards via the existing webhook flow.

inspection_notes.description: Optional inspection notes recorded on the return (max 2000 chars).

return_id.description: UUID of the return to accept. Acceptance refunds the buyer immediately (idempotent).

tools.name: seller_accept_return
tools.title: Seller accept return

tools.description: Reject a return after inspection. inspection_notes is required. Refuses if the return has already refunded.

inspection_notes.description: Reason for rejection, shared with the buyer (1-2000 chars).

return_id.description: UUID of the return to reject. Rejection is terminal: no refund is issued.

tools.name: seller_reject_return
tools.title: Seller reject return

tools.description: List reviews left on this seller's orders, paginated. Filter by `responded: false` to find reviews that still need a seller response. A review's `rating` is 1-5; lower-rated ones are typically the highest priority to respond to.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor.

tools.name: seller_list_reviews
tools.title: Seller list reviews

tools.description: Post the seller's response to a review. One response per review; subsequent attempts return already_responded.

review_id.description: UUID of the review to respond to. Each review allows one seller response.

text.description: Public response text shown under the review (1-2000 chars).

tools.name: seller_respond_to_review
tools.title: Seller respond to review
